neighbours.label: The opening word of a new sentence or quoted line that continues a sequence ('Then', 'Visitors also', 'Before ...'), vs the same content as a single run-on clause
fire:
> First we would clean the data.
> Then I could build a small model to test the idea.

> I would sketch the layout on paper.
> Then we could pick the colours together.
Before entering the lab, students put on goggles. Teachers also check every bench.
Before boarding, passengers show their tickets. Children also need a seat belt.

> We would book the hall in March.
> Then I could send the invitations to everyone.
Before cooking, chefs wash every vegetable. Kitchen staff also clean the boards.

> I would read the contract tonight.
> Then we could sign it on Monday morning.
Before swimming, guests take a shower. Lifeguards also watch the deep end.
quiet: We would clean the data first and build a small model to test the idea.
I would sketch the layout on paper and we could pick the colours together.
Students put on goggles before entering the lab and teachers check every bench.
Passengers show their tickets before boarding and children need a seat belt.
We would book the hall in March and send the invitations to everyone.
Chefs wash every vegetable before cooking and kitchen staff clean the boards.
I would read the contract tonight so we could sign it on Monday morning.
Guests take a shower before swimming while lifeguards watch the deep end.
